name: ComputerUse.space

modes.label: ThinkCentre 8 GB planned
modes.note: Advertised $24.99 per 30 days, not a 730-hour month. Host has 8 GB installed RAM and planned 80 GB customer storage; guest RAM and CPU unknown. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: ThinkCentre 16 GB planned
modes.note: Advertised $39.99 per 30 days. Host has 16 GB installed RAM and planned 150 GB customer storage; guest RAM and CPU unknown. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: ThinkCentre annual prepay (planned)
modes.commit_note: $239.90 / $383.90 prepaid per calendar year (= $19.99 / $31.99 per month); 20% off twelve 30-day payments

plans.name: Prelaunch reservation terms
plans.note: No purchasable inventory or live payments (/api/v1/stock: available 0, purchases_enabled false). Rental targets $24.99/$39.99 per 30 days, prepaid credit, auto-renew from balance; annual prepay $239.90/$383.90 per calendar year. Up to 100 computers per order.

features.ip_note: Desktops run as Proxmox VMs on rented owner hosts (Lenovo ThinkCentre), with a Hetzner relay fallback for streaming; egress IP type undocumented. Prelaunch: customer rentals pending.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Explicit prelaunch: account/management APIs and a Linux owner pilot exist, but customer rentals, live payments and verified inventory are not open. Modes are beta-only.

Installed host RAM is not fully available guest RAM. Customers do not receive Proxmox host administration. Windows readiness, editing performance, backups, proxies and storage add-ons need verification.

Billing is prepaid credit (top-ups); each rental auto-renews from balance every 30 days; insufficient credit queues suspension. Paid term starts when provisioning is confirmed ready. 30-day term means ~12.17 renewals per calendar year (1.4% above a 730h month).
Windows is listed as plan software in the stock API (Standard: Windows; Creator: Windows, CapCut) but docs say Linux is the initial target and a Windows surcharge has not been finalized.
Terminal/file API, file transfers, templates/clone/resize, proxies, NAS/S3 backups, SSO/SLA are not deployed (roadmap/proposal). Proxies, storage upgrades, paid software billed separately (unpriced).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: | Reboot or stop | Disk remains; running processes are not retained |
snapshot_auto.note: Stop/reboot only keeps the local SSD guest disk (that is persistent_disk); no automatic snapshot or memory checkpoint on stop/idle. There is no idle auto-stop at all: rentals are always-on 30-day dedicated hosts. Backups (NAS/S3) are an architecture proposal only.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: | Templates, clone, resize, multi-screen | Roadmap | Capacity-aware runtime implementation |
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint in the OpenAPI file, which the docs say lists exactly the implemented handlers ('All paths in that document correspond to current handlers.', https://computeruse.space/docs-source/api.md). Templates/cloning are roadmap; a clone would need a second physical host. Proxmox VM snapshots exist under the hood (mentioned only in cleanup/retention context) but customers get no Proxmox administration.

harness_api.quote: | Managed model routing / agent threads | Roadmap | Provider integration, metering and retention |
harness_api.note: The opposite direction exists: a stdio MCP bridge (python -m computeruse.mcp) and REST API let an external agent (Boardly, OpenClaw, Hermes) manage rentals and drive the desktop via screenshots/mouse/keyboard leases. Nothing starts or streams an agent harness inside the guest; no terminal/exec API either ('Terminal/file API and audio | Not deployed'). Boardly (separate product) has take-over/give-back of the desktop, not a harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: All paths in that document correspond to current handlers. Planned runtime APIs are documented separately and are not included as if implemented.
egress_allowlist.note: Implemented API has no network-policy endpoints (groups: accounts, keys, rentals, billing, proxies catalog/quote, admin, desktops). Operator-side tenant isolation is only a design goal: 'Each customer guest should have its own isolated network boundary. Deny access to the operator's LAN, host/hypervisor services, other guests and storage administration.' (proxies.md); pilot runs on an unmanaged switch. No customer-configurable allow/deny list.

egress_http_rules.quote: All paths in that document correspond to current handlers. Planned runtime APIs are documented separately and are not included as if implemented.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP-level egress rules implemented or planned in docs. Supplier-backed outbound proxies are 'Catalog/quote foundation · Supplier activation pending' (a quote does not attach a proxy); these are IP-rotation proxies, not policy rules.

secret_proxy.quote: Agents still need model-provider credentials and budgets. ComputerUse's rental price does not pay for unlimited tokens. Prefer short-lived scoped secrets, task budgets and approval for consequential actions.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy and no secret store. Hosted agents keep their API keys inside the guest ('Its state, channels, API keys and learned skills then become part of the customer workspace'); templates doc says 'Inject customer secrets at provisioning time' (roadmap). Managed model routing is roadmap. No non-HTTP coverage.

volume_attach.quote: | NAS/S3 storage and disaster recovery | Architecture proposal | Hardware/provider configuration and restore drills |
volume_attach.note: Only the fixed local-SSD guest disk (80 GiB Standard / 150 GiB Creator). storage-backups.md: 'Architecture proposal · No storage provider connected'. Storage upgrades mentioned elsewhere as separately billed add-ons but unpriced/not implemented.

volume_shared.quote: A NAS can store image backups, approved customer file shares and media projects. Give every tenant a separate authorized share and quota. Do not mount a global share inside every guest.
volume_shared.note: Proposal only (page status 'Architecture proposal · No storage provider connected'); a per-tenant NAS share could in future be mounted by several of one customer's computers, but nothing is implemented. virtual-computers.md: NAS/S3 'Neither is automatically a shared customer folder.'
